Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation with Maria at Enterprise Retail, we put together a private offer that we believe will accelerate adoption across their retail accounts. High-level ask below and attached is a starter draft of the private offer and the ratecard (see attachments).

Summary of CloudZen ask:
- 20% upfront marketplace commission to CloudZen for the first 12 months (vs standard 15%).
- Add a quarterly rebate schedule: if cumulative usage from Maria's tenants > $120k ARR in Q1, CloudZen receives a one-time $12k rebate credit applied to the next invoice.
- Payment terms: Net60 to align with the buyer's procurement process (they cannot do net30).
- Termination carve: buyer requests a 90-day right-to-exit with pro-rated credits; CloudZen wants a one-time early-termination fee waived for strategic pilot.
- Special rev-share tier: sliding scale down to 12% after $1.2M ARR threshold for the account.

We know some of these deviate from your standard marketplace terms (rev-share floor / payment terms). Could you advise on internal approval process and whether Redwood would consider a temporary commission uplift and the rebate structure?

Attachments: CloudZen_PrivateOffer_Draft.pdf; CloudZen_Ratecard.xlsx

Appreciate a quick turnaround — buyer is hoping to close pilot procurement next week.

Best,
Ariana
Head of Partnerships
CloudZen

Forwarding CloudZen's proposal — requesting deal-desk + revenue sign-off.

Quick context: Enterprise Retail (contact: Maria Solis) is a strategic vertical anchor for CloudZen. They want Net60 and the rebate mechanics to encourage expansion into new stores. CloudZen is asking for a short-term commission uplift (20%) and a one-off pilot waiver on termination fee. My recommended position is:
- Approve commission uplift to 18% for first 6 months only (revenue impact modeled at ~$9k/mo).
- Rebate can be approved but needs a capped $15k total liability and clear metric triggers (we should codify thresholds in the contract).
- Payment terms: Net60 is acceptable ONLY if we secure an upfront pre-pay for month 1 or an ACH/PO milestone; otherwise stick to Net30.
- No full waiver on termination fees — allow buyer a 90-day pilot window but require a minimum usage commitment (30% of forecast) or IR (initial run) credit recapture.

Karthik / Marissa / Laura — can you review attached draft and provide explicit sign-off or a set of exceptions we can offer? Buyer timeline: wants to execute by 1/11.

Jonas Weber

Thanks for the flag, Jonas. I reviewed the draft and ran pencil on expected gross margins and commission leakage under the two asks. Key items from deal-desk/legal/finance POV:

1) Commission uplift to 20% is a non-starter. We can do a time-boxed uplift to 18% for 3 months, but it must be: (a) tied to an executed SOW from Maria's team (pilot acceptance), and (b) capped to $30k total commission uplift across the account.

2) Rebate schedule: acceptable if we add a payback clause. If the buyer consumes < 70% of the forecasted usage after Q1, rebate will be clawed back pro rata from CloudZen's subsequent commissions. Also we must cap Redwood's exposure to $15k as Jonas suggested.

3) Net60: finance will not accept standard Net60 for a first-time private offer without a credit application and PO. We can accept Net60 only with a signed credit application + ACH mandate and a 25% upfront deposit. No exceptions.

4) Termination / pilot: we can approve a 90-day pilot window but require a minimum revenue commitment (MRR floor equivalent to $5k/mo) or else CloudZen's waived termination fee will be recouped via a final invoice.

5) Legal redlines: add explicit language that the rev-share sliding scale resets per fiscal year and is evaluated on aggregate Redwood invoices to the buyer (not CloudZen internal invoices). Also include audit rights limited to once per 12 months to protect platform data privacy.

If Marissa is comfortable with these constraints, I recommend we escalate to Marissa for exec sign-off (revenue tolerance + commission carve).

Karthik
Senior Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference
